title: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, TYPE 2A1
alt_titles: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, TYPE 2A1
HEREDITARY MOTOR AND SENSORY NEUROPATHY IIA1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene on chromosome 1p35-p36.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: CMT2A1 is the current name for CMT2A as described here.

checks.claim: The KIF1B gene is located on chromosome 1p35-p36.
checks.evidence_quote: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A was previously mapped to an interval containing KIF1B.
checks.explanation: The 1p35-p36 location does not appear in the abstract. It is standard nomenclature, which the rules accept as supported.

paragraphs.text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy. Age of onset varies, and nerve conduction velocity is normal or slightly reduced. CMT2 differs from CMT1 both pathologically and genetically (Ben Othmane et al., 1993).

checks.evidence_quote: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy

checks.claim: The age of onset of CMT2 varies.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by variable age of onset

checks.claim: Nerve conduction velocity in CMT2 is normal or slightly reduced.
checks.evidence_quote: normal or slightly diminished nerve conduction velocity

checks.claim: CMT2 differs from CMT1 pathologically.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT2 is pathologically and genetically distinct from CMT type 1 (CMT1).

checks.claim: CMT2 differs from CMT1 genetically.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT2 is pathologically and genetically distinct from CMT type 1 (CMT1).

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) described the clinical features of CMT2A in 2 Japanese families. The posterior and anterior tibial muscles were weak to a similar degree. Tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper limbs but were reduced or absent in the lower limbs. The peripheral nerves were not enlarged. Only 20% of affected individuals had mild sensory disturbance.

paragraphs.text: The families with CMT2 studied by Hentati et al. (1992) and Ben Othmane et al. (1993) showed autosomal dominant inheritance. In Kif1b knockout mice, heterozygous animals developed progressive muscle weakness (Zhao et al., 2001).

checks.claim: The families with CMT2 studied by Hentati et al. (1992) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: The autosomal dominant forms of hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies include the hypertrophic form (CMT1) and the neuronal form of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).
checks.explanation: The abstract frames the study as being about the autosomal dominant forms, CMT1 and CMT2, and analyzes two CMT2 pedigrees. It does not describe how the disease was passed down in each pedigree, so autosomal dominant inheritance in the studied families is implied by the study's framing rather than shown in detail. Only the abstract was available.

checks.claim: The families with CMT2 studied by Ben Othmane et al. (1993) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the families studied were autosomal dominant CMT2 families.

checks.claim: In Kif1b knockout mice, heterozygous animals developed progressive muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that heterozygous KIF1B knockout mice develop progressive muscle weakness.

paragraphs.text: Hentati et al. (1992) studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees and excluded the CMT2 locus from the region of chromosome 17 where CMT1A maps (lod score -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58). In a CMT1 pedigree studied alongside them, they confirmed linkage to CMT1A (lod +3.67 at theta = 0.00). The CMT2 pedigrees also gave negative lod scores for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B (lod -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).

checks.evidence_quote: Studying one CMT1 and two CMT2 pedigrees
checks.explanation: The abstract states that two CMT2 pedigrees were studied.

checks.evidence_quote: we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps
checks.explanation: The locus, marker, lod score and theta all match the abstract.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) confirmed linkage to CMT1A in a CMT1 pedigree studied alongside the CMT2 pedigrees, with a lod score of +3.67 at theta = 0.00.
checks.evidence_quote: Studying one CMT1 and two CMT2 pedigrees, we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps (Z = +3.67 at theta = 0.00).
checks.explanation: The lod of +3.67 at theta = 0.00 for the CMT1A region is reported in a study that included one CMT1 pedigree, so it follows that this pedigree gave the positive linkage. The abstract does not name the marker used.

checks.claim: The CMT2 pedigrees studied by Hentati et al. (1992) gave negative lod scores for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B, with a lod score of -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61.

checks.explanation: The negative lod score, theta and marker D1S61 all match the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) performed linkage analysis in 6 large families with autosomal dominant CMT2. They found linkage to the microsatellite markers D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199, which lie in the distal part of the short arm of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis of the linked families placed the CMT2A gene most likely between D1S244 and D1S228. The odds that the gene lay within this interval rather than outside it were approximately 70:1.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) performed linkage analysis in 2 Japanese families with CMT2. The highest cumulative multipoint lod score was 3.69, at marker D1S244, consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.

checks.claim: In the 2 Japanese CMT2 families, Saito et al. (1997) obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at marker D1S244.

checks.claim: The linkage results of Saito et al. (1997) in 2 Japanese CMT2 families were consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.

paragraphs.text: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous. They found that the CMT2 gene was not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: The present study therefore provides evidence for genetic heterogeneity between the hypertrophic and the neuronal forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) found that the CMT2 gene was not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrates that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped to date.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) applied admixture analysis of two-point lod scores to 6 CMT2 families and found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity, which multipoint admixture analysis supported. The posterior probabilities of being of the linked type were 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 for families DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523, respectively. The authors suggested that at least 2 different genes can cause the CMT2 phenotype.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) applied admixture analysis of two-point lod scores to 6 CMT2 families and found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant evidence for heterogeneity was found using admixture analysis and the two-point lod scores.
checks.explanation: The six families come from the same study.

checks.claim: Multipoint admixture analysis by Ben Othmane et al. (1993) supported genetic heterogeneity in CMT2.
checks.evidence_quote: Admixture analyses using the multipoint results for the markers D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199 supported the two-point findings.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) found posterior probabilities of being of the linked type of 1.0 for family DUK662, 0.98 for family DUK1241, and 0.88 for family 1523.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families, DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523 gave posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type.
checks.explanation: The values and family IDs match the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: The CMT2B and CMT2D loci were excluded by the results of linkage analysis performed using markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) found a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene in patients with CMT2A. CMT2A had previously been mapped to an interval that contains KIF1B. The authors studied KIF1B-beta, an isoform of the kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B that differs from KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain; KIF1B had previously been shown to transport mitochondria. Zhao et al. (2001) concluded that defects in axonal transport caused by a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.

checks.claim: KIF1B-beta differs from KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain.

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) reported that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from apnea caused by defects of the nervous system. Knockout neurons that were dying in culture could be rescued by expressing the KIF1B-beta isoform. Heterozygous mice were defective in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and developed progressive muscle weakness similar to that seen in human neuropathies.

checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.

checks.claim: Dying Kif1b knockout neurons in culture could be rescued by expressing the KIF1B-beta isoform.
checks.evidence_quote: Death of knockout neurons in culture can be rescued by expression of the beta isoform.

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b knockout mice were defective in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors.
checks.evidence_quote: The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b knockout mice developed progressive muscle weakness similar to that seen in human neuropathies.
checks.evidence_quote: suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.
